gate.dispatchTitle: {count, plural, one {# dispatch awaiting approval} other {# dispatches awaiting approval}}
gate.disbursementTitle: {count, plural, one {# release awaiting approval} other {# releases awaiting approval}}

degraded.title: Some data is unavailable
degraded.agentExplanation: The agent service is not reachable. Incidents below are ordered by the deterministic score, not by a model. Nothing here is an assisted ranking.
degraded.backendExplanation: Showing the last picture received. It is {age} old and may not reflect the current situation.
degraded.reasoningExplanation: Nothing recorded a reason for this plan, so there is no factor breakdown and no unservable list to show. That is not the same as the agent having weighed nothing: a plan proposed outside the triage agent carries no reasoning at all. Decide from the incidents and the route below, or reject and ask for a re-plan.

cop.title: Common operating picture
cop.queueEmpty: No incidents in the current filter
cop.queueEmptyHint: The filter may be excluding them. Clear it to see the whole queue.
cop.contextEmptyHint: Choose a row in the queue to see its reports, its triage factors and its audit trail.
cop.unplaceable: {count, plural, one {# incident has no coordinate and is not on the map} other {# incidents have no coordinate and are not on the map}}
cop.layersNotBuilt: Shelters with occupancy are not drawn: nothing on this platform holds shelter positions or capacity. Delivery-gap shading is on the alert delivery screen, where an alert scopes it.
cop.noFactors: No factor breakdown was recorded for this incident.
cop.auditEmpty: Nothing has been recorded against this incident yet.
cop.auditUnavailable: The audit trail could not be read. This is not an empty history.
cop.reportsEmpty: No report is linked to this incident yet
cop.reportsEmptyHint: Reports link as they arrive and as dedup matches them. Nothing is hidden by a filter.
cop.reportsUnavailable: The linked reports could not be read.
cop.transcriptionAccepted: Above the review threshold, so it was acted on automatically.
cop.heldForReview: Below the review threshold, so a person must read it before it is acted on.
cop.audioNotPlayable: A recording exists but cannot be played here: the object store is not wired, so this is a key rather than a link.
cop.audioUnsupported: Your browser cannot play this recording.
cop.dedupHint: A wrong merge hides a second emergency behind the first. Open either to split them.
cop.layerDivisionsHint: Fetched one division at a time, only for divisions with an incident in this queue.
cop.respondersUnplaced: {count, plural, one {# responder has reported no position and is not on the map} other {# responders have reported no position and are not on the map}}.

dispatch.title: Dispatch approval
dispatch.queueEmpty: Nothing is waiting for a dispatch decision
dispatch.queueEmptyHint: Plans appear here when the triage agent proposes one. Nothing is hidden by a filter.
dispatch.routeUnavailable: No route geometry on this plan
dispatch.factors: Why these incidents are ranked here
dispatch.unservable: {count, plural, one {# incident this plan does not cover} other {# incidents this plan does not cover}}
dispatch.unservableNone: Every incident in scope is covered by this plan.
dispatch.unservableWarning: These incidents were considered and left out. Read them before approving.
dispatch.totpHint: Six digits from your authenticator app. Required to approve.
dispatch.totpIncomplete: Enter all six digits to approve.
dispatch.approveConfirm: This sends responders towards a hazard. There is no undo.
dispatch.planNotFoundHint: It may have been decided already. Return to the queue to see its status.
dispatch.blockedSegmentsNotBuilt: Blocked road segments are not drawn. This platform holds no road network, so the line joins the stops in order rather than following a road.
dispatch.lowConfidenceStops: {count, plural, one {# stop has a location the platform cannot fully trust} other {# stops have locations the platform cannot fully trust}}.
dispatch.whyRanked: Why these incidents are ranked here
dispatch.whyRankedHint: Expanded on purpose. If you have to click to see the reasoning, you stop reading it.
dispatch.rationale: The agent's account of this plan
dispatch.noFactorsForIncident: This plan's reasoning does not mention this incident.
dispatch.unservableHint: No responder could be routed to these. They are not covered by this plan, and approving it does not send anybody to them.
dispatch.reasoningMissing: No reasoning was recorded for this plan

disbursement.title: Release approval
disbursement.queueEmpty: Nothing is waiting for a release decision
disbursement.queueEmptyHint: Entitlements appear here once they carry every required approval.
disbursement.householdRefOnly: Reference only. The approver does not need the name and does not get it.
disbursement.evidenceNone: No photographs attached to this assessment
disbursement.grievanceOpen: An open grievance blocks this release
disbursement.grievanceExplanation: This entitlement has an unresolved grievance. The release endpoint will refuse it, and it should: the household has said something is wrong and nobody has answered yet.
disbursement.anomalyExplanation: A pattern in this division was flagged for review. It is not a finding and it names nobody. Read the innocent explanations before deciding.
disbursement.segregationOk: You are neither the assessor nor an approver of this entitlement.
disbursement.segregationBlocked: You cannot release this: you are recorded as {role} on it.
disbursement.releaseConfirm: This moves money. There is no undo; a mistake is corrected with a compensating entry.
disbursement.simulated: Every payment rail in this phase is a mock. References start MOCK-.
disbursement.traceEmpty: No working was recorded for this entitlement. Nobody can check the figure, so do not sign it: raise it instead.
disbursement.calculationHint: Every recorded step, in the order it was applied. A step this screen does not recognise is still shown.

errors.title: Something went wrong
errors.generic: The request did not complete. The correlation ID below identifies it in the server logs.
errors.forbidden: You do not have access to this
errors.forbiddenHint: Your role does not cover this area or this action.
errors.stepUpHint: This action needs a second factor from the last five minutes.

auth.totpPrompt: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
auth.failedHint: Check the username and password and try again.
auth.emailHint: The address your account was created with.
auth.stepUpWhy: You are signed in. Committing a dispatch or releasing money needs more than that: it needs proof that the person at this keyboard right now is you. An unattended workstation is the realistic attack on a platform that sends responders and moves money.
auth.stepUpWindow: A confirmation lasts {minutes} minutes. After that the next gate asks again.
auth.stepUpFailed: That code was not accepted. Codes change every 30 seconds, so try the current one.
auth.stepUpNotAuthorisation: This confirms who you are, not what you may do. Every gate re-checks both when you reach it.

incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.emptyHint: Clear the filter to see the whole list. Nothing is hidden by scope here.
incidents.locationLowHint: A point with low confidence is not trusted for dispatch. It still counts towards the division, and a responder needs a person to confirm where it is.
incidents.notFoundHint: It may have been merged into another. Return to the list.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.emptyHint: An alert is drafted from a published template. Templates are seeded as DRAFT and need a human signature in each language first.
alerts.gapsHint: Divisions with low confirmed delivery, worst first. This is where to send a vehicle with a loudhailer.
alerts.gapsNone: No division is below the delivery threshold
alerts.gapsNoneHint: Every targeted division has confirmed delivery above the threshold. That is not the same as everyone having heard it.
alerts.noDenominator: Counts are always shown with what they are a fraction of.
alerts.dryRunHint: Asks what this alert would do. Sends nothing.
alerts.dryRunFirst: Send is unavailable until a dry run has been performed. Sending a life-safety message to an unknown number of people is the failure this step exists to stop.
alerts.estimatedCostHint: Indicative, per message. Not a tariff.
alerts.exceedsCap: This alert targets {targeted} people, above the {cap} cap
alerts.exceedsCapHint: Check the area selection first. If it is right, say why this send should proceed anyway. The reason is stored with the dispatch.
alerts.overrideReasonHint: Required. At least a few words, and it is read afterwards.
alerts.sendConfirmBody: There is no recall. A cancellation is a second message, not an undo.
alerts.sendBlockedByOverride: Give a reason for exceeding the cap.
alerts.notDispatchable: This alert is not in a state that can be dispatched.
alerts.signoffRequired: A human must sign this off first
alerts.signoffHint: It carries free text outside the approved templates, so a named person signs before it can go anywhere.
alerts.quietHoursInactive: Quiet hours are not in effect
alerts.quietHoursRule: Between {start}:00 and {end}:00 Colombo, only class {level} and above sends on {channels}. Below that, those channels are held.
alerts.quietHoursBypass: This alert is at or above the class that sends anyway. It will wake people.
alerts.quietHoursDeferred: Those channels will be held until {time} Colombo. The other channels go now.
alerts.gapMapHint: Shaded by confirmed fraction. The table below carries the order, and the order is the instruction.
alerts.gapsUnplaceable: {count, plural, one {# division could not be placed on the map and appears in the table only} other {# divisions could not be placed on the map and appear in the table only}}.

audit.title: Audit
audit.ledgerEmptyHint: No entries have been written yet. Nothing is filtered out of this view.
audit.anomaliesEmptyHint: Nothing has been flagged for review, or every flag has been disposed of.
audit.disposeNoteHint: Required for every outcome, including a false positive. A flag closed without reasoning tells the next reviewer nothing.
audit.neverNames: A flag is a pattern, not a finding. It names nobody.
audit.readsAreAudited: Every read on this page is itself recorded in the audit log, including this one.
audit.fromSeqHint: Where this page starts. The ledger is paged, not searched.
audit.pageWindow: Showing {shown} entries from sequence {from}. This is one page of the ledger, not the whole of it.
audit.anchorsEmpty: No anchor has been published yet
audit.anchorsEmptyHint: An anchor is written once a day over that day's entries. None has run against this database.
audit.noExternalAnchor: Not written to an object store
audit.unanchoredDays: {count, plural, one {# day has a Merkle root that was never written to an external object store} other {# days have Merkle roots that were never written to an external object store}}. Those days are verifiable only against a database an operator controls, which is a weaker claim than an intact chain suggests.
audit.verifyCliHint: Verify this chain independently, without access to this console or its source. The hashing scheme is published with the anchors.

review.title: Review queue
review.emptyHint: Low-confidence transcriptions and flagged reports appear here.

grievances.title: Grievances
grievances.emptyHint: A grievance is raised by a household, by SMS or through an officer.
grievances.slaDoesNotReset: The clock started when the household complained and an assignment does not restart it.
grievances.assignTitle: Route this to a DS division
grievances.assignHint: The office that will answer it. Assigning does not answer it and does not stop the clock.
grievances.dsDivisionInvalid: A DS division code looks like LK-11-03.
grievances.resolveHint: The text below is sent to the household. Write it in all three languages, because they will read it in one of them.
grievances.rejectionNeedsReason: A household told only that their claim was rejected has learned nothing they can act on, and cannot tell a decision from a mistake. Say why, and say what they can do next.
grievances.missingLanguages: Still needed in {languages}. A household that reads only one of the three would receive nothing.

notBuilt.title: This screen is not built yet
notBuilt.body: It is named in build file 20 and it does not exist. Nothing is hidden behind it and nothing is broken — there is simply no page here yet. The handoff lists which routes are outstanding.

compose.title: Compose an alert
compose.templateHint: Only published templates can be dispatched.
compose.noPublishedHint: All twelve seeded templates are drafts. Before an alert can be dispatched a human must sign each language and then publish it. That is the gate working, not a missing seed.
compose.awaitingSignature: awaiting a signature in Sinhala or Tamil
compose.freeTextForcesSignoff: Anything here is outside the reviewed template, so the alert goes to PENDING_SIGNOFF and a human reads it before it can be dispatched. Say what the templates cannot; just know it will wait for a person.
compose.divisionsHint: Comma separated, e.g. LK-11-03-045. Area selection on the map is not built.
compose.dryRunRequired: A dry run is required before sending
compose.dryRunExplanation: The confirm step shows the exact target count, the per-channel breakdown and the per-language split. Sending a life-safety message to an unknown number of people is not something this console will let you do.
compose.overLimitBlocks: One of the three renderings needs more than two segments. Shorten it before drafting: the language that runs long is the one whose community gets the warning last and incomplete.
compose.hazardEventHint: Which event this alert is about.
compose.noHazardEvents: No open hazard event. An alert has to name the event it is about, and one is declared by the forecast agent or by DMC — not from this console.
compose.drafted: Draft created: {reference}. It still needs sign-off and a dry run before it can be sent.
compose.areaSearchHint: A code or a name in any of the three scripts.
compose.areaSearchPrompt: Type at least two characters. There are about 14,000 divisions, so this searches rather than lists.
compose.areaNoMatchHint: Try a code such as LK-11-03, or a name in Sinhala, Tamil or English.
compose.areaPolygonNotBuilt: Drawing a polygon that snaps to boundaries is not built. It needs every candidate boundary in the viewport, and geometry is served one division at a time out of about 14,000. A lasso that snapped to nothing would be worse than none.

chain.title: Chain verification
chain.subtitle: Recompute the hash chain and compare it against the published daily anchors. This is where the claim that a record cannot be edited after it is written gets tested rather than read.
chain.verifyRangeHint: Leave both blank to check the whole chain. A result always names the range it covers, so a partial check is never mistaken for a whole one.
chain.diverged: Diverged — the chain does not recompute
chain.anchorsHint: One Merkle root per day, each chained to the day before, so removing a whole day is as detectable as altering one row inside it.
chain.noAnchorsHint: An anchor is written once a day has entries to anchor.
chain.noExternalAnchor: {count, plural, one {# day has no external anchor} other {# days have no external anchor}}
chain.noExternalAnchorHint: The root is computed and chained, but it has not been written to storage outside this system. Until it is, the chain is verifiable against a database the operator controls — which is a weaker claim than it looks, and the external anchor is the half that survives an operator rewriting it.

assessments.title: Assessments
assessments.readOnly: Read-only. Creating an assessment needs photographs, GPS and an offline queue, which is the Field Companion’s job — a form here would be a way of entering damage figures nobody stood in front of.
assessments.emptyHint: Assessments arrive from the Field Companion, or by sync when a handset regains signal.
assessments.newTitle: File an assessment from a desk
assessments.newSubtitle: The Field Companion is the tool for this. Use this screen when the handset is dead, lost, or was never issued.
assessments.deskFiledNoPhotos: No photographs. An assessment filed here carries no evidence, and the approver at the money gate will see none.
assessments.deskFiledNoPosition: No position. The check that flags an assessment filed thirty kilometres from the division cannot run on this record, because there is no honest coordinate to record from a desk.
assessments.deskFiledUseApp: If the handset works, use it. Everything above is available there and this record will be weaker than one filed in front of the house.
assessments.householdHint: By reference code. This platform holds no household names.
assessments.noHouseholds: No household is registered in this division.
assessments.subcategoryHint: Optional. A short note the schedule line does not cover.
assessments.costEstimateHint: In rupees. The entitlement is calculated from the schedule, not from this figure alone.
assessments.filedHint: It is now waiting to be accepted, and an entitlement is calculated from it once it is.
assessments.alreadyFiledHint: This form was submitted before and the stored record was returned. Nothing was filed twice.

admin.title: Administration
admin.templatesHint: A template needs a native signature in Sinhala and in Tamil before it can be published, and no alert can be dispatched from an unpublished one. This is the gate; it is not a formality.
admin.noTemplatesHint: Templates are created by seeding or through POST /templates.
admin.needsBothSignatures: Publication needs both signatures. The server refuses without them, and so does a database predicate.
admin.schedulesHint: Read-only. A schedule is what every entitlement is calculated from; changing one from a console during an incident would silently re-price work already done. Versions are added by migration.
admin.noSchedulesHint: Schedules arrive with the seed data or by migration.
admin.usersHint: Who holds which role, where, and whether they have a second factor. An approver without one cannot pass a gate.
admin.rolesHint: Read from the same table the platform authorises against, not from a description of it.
admin.rolesReadOnly: Roles are defined in code and cannot be edited here. A console that could change what a role means would be editing the authorisation model during an incident.
admin.noUsersHint: Clear the filters to see everyone. Nothing is hidden by permission here.
admin.manageHint: Granting and revoking both need a second factor. A role grant is how somebody acquires the power to release money.
admin.grantAreaHint: LK for national, LK-11 for a district, LK-11-03 for a DS division, LK-11-03-045 for a GN division.
admin.grantAreaInvalid: That code is not the shape this level requires.
admin.grantReasonHint: Required, and read afterwards. A permission change nobody can explain is one nobody can review.
admin.humanGateWarning: This role can commit a dispatch or release money. Grant it deliberately.
admin.totpHint: Six digits. Required to grant or revoke.
admin.scenarioNotHere: The scenario controls are not driven from this console.
admin.scenarioWhy: gov-mock impersonates the Department of Meteorology, NBRO, the NDRSC and three payment rails. It is deliberately absent from the service map behind the gateway, so nothing here can advance its clock or inject a failure. A console that could would be a console that can make the platform believe a cyclone made landfall.
admin.scenarioMock: Run these from a terminal, deliberately. Every response from that port carries a mock-data header.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.subtitle: Entitlements waiting for a signature. Oldest first: the household that has waited longest is the one to reach first.
approvals.empty: Nothing is waiting for an approval
approvals.emptyHint: An entitlement appears here once an assessment has been accepted and valued.
approvals.totpHint: Six digits from your authenticator app. An approval is the signature the money gate relies on.
approvals.notARelease: Approving is not releasing. A different person confirms the money should move, and the service refuses a release by whoever approved it.
approvals.twoLevelsBecause: Above the District threshold, so it needs both signatures. The service decides this, not the console.
approvals.oneLevelBecause: At or below the District threshold, so one DS signature is enough.
approvals.noApprovalsYet: No signature has been recorded yet.

forecast.title: Impact forecast
forecast.subtitle: What is expected, where, and how long there is to act on it.
forecast.divisionsEvacuateHint: Class 4. Only NBRO's own evacuate threshold reaches it.
forecast.soonestHint: The clock you are working against, not an average.
forecast.confidenceHint: Confidence is about the inputs available, not about how bad it will be.
forecast.driversHint: Every recorded driver, including any this screen has not seen before. A forecast with no account of what moved it is not reviewable.
forecast.historyHint: When the class first rose, and how far ahead. This is what answers "did we see this coming".
forecast.historyUnavailable: The earlier runs could not be read.
forecast.selectDivision: Open a division to read its drivers and its earlier runs.
forecast.empty: No division is forecast at or above this class
forecast.emptyHint: Lower the class filter to see the quieter divisions. Nothing is hidden.
forecast.triggersHint: Conditions agreed before the event. A fired trigger always says what it did, even when that was nothing.
forecast.triggersEmpty: No triggers are set for this event
forecast.triggersEmptyHint: Triggers are agreed in advance and loaded with the scenario. None has been recorded here.
